narrative.overview:
The Default theme is the room everyone starts in: friendly, unpretentious, and deliberately quiet, built entirely on stock Bootstrap 5.3 behavior with a light coat of Nunito and Nexus Sky Blue. It exists so that the site's optional theme packs — Excelsior's black-and-neon terminal look, Halloween, Hotdog, Xmas, the legacy Nexus2 skin — are the ones that get to be visually loud. The Default theme's job is to stay out of the way: legible, warm, a little plain by design, and explicitly not sleek corporate SaaS.

Components come across as tidy and a little playful rather than austere: standard Bootstrap bones (navbar, cards, breadcrumbs, buttons) carry a few hand-placed touches — pill-shaped chat bubbles, icon-accented nav links, a quote-mark blockquote treatment — that give the app personality without asking it to look bolder than it is. This is a passion project for a small, invested community; the visual system should feel sturdy and familiar to a returning user, never like a relaunch.
keyCharacteristics: Cool, mist-and-slate neutral canvas with one confident accent (Nexus Sky Blue) doing most of the color work.
Stock Bootstrap grid, spacing, and component shapes — no attempt to hide or restyle the framework.
Flat by default; the rare soft shadow marks a quote or a message bubble, never generic 'raised UI.'
Personality lives in small, specific details (icon sizing, chat bubbles, blockquote quote-mark), not in a system-wide visual statement.
The Default theme is one of several installable Bootstrap-variable themes; nothing here should assume it's the only skin the app will ever wear.

rules.name: The Readable-Text Rule
rules.body: Every theme color has an explicit, hand-picked text color rather than relying on Bootstrap's automatic contrast calculation. Don't remove the explicit overrides in favor of automatic contrast.

rules.name: The One Signature Blue Rule
rules.body: Nexus Sky Blue is the only color that should read as 'the site's color' — new UI should reach for $primary before introducing a new hue.

rules.name: The AA-Or-Darker Rule
rules.body: $primary, $success, and $info are calibrated so their white-text pairing (and $primary as link text on $neutral-bg) clears 4.5:1. Re-check contrast against both white and #f5f8fa before changing these hues.

rules.name: The Single-Typeface Rule
rules.body: Don't introduce a second font family for emphasis or distinction — weight and size carry all the hierarchy this system needs.

rules.name: The Flat-Unless-Quoted Rule
rules.body: Don't add a shadow to a card, button, or nav element to make it feel important. Shadow is reserved for content that is literally being quoted back to the reader.

dos: Do keep every new color decision inside the existing $theme-colors map so it survives a theme switch to Excelsior, Halloween, Hotdog, Xmas, or Nexus2 without extra work.
Do give every new colored button/badge variant an explicit text-color override rather than trusting automatic contrast.
Do use the three fixed icon-size classes (icon_mini / icon_medium / icon_large) for any new Heroicon usage.
Do treat shadow as a signal reserved for quoted/conversational content, not general UI weight.
donts: Don't hardcode a new hex color for chat, badges, or alerts when a $theme-colors entry already covers the intent — this drifted once for the chat bubbles and was fixed by switching to $success/$primary.
Don't introduce a second typeface. Nunito plus weight variation is the entire type system.
Don't add drop shadows to cards, nav, or buttons to signal elevation or importance.

Don't assume the Default theme's exact colors, radius, or font are load-bearing outside it — the override mechanism used by Excelsior, Halloween, Hotdog, Xmas, and Nexus2 is a first-class product feature, not a shortcut to work around.
